topic: What trade-offs exist between maintaining axial ratio below 3dB and achieving wide-angle beam steering up to 45°?
consensus_response: Maintaining axial ratio below 3dB while achieving wide-angle beam steering up to 45° results in a trade-off between reduced maximum gain, increased scanning loss, and compromised polarization purity. The use of phase-delay cells (PD) offers better axial ratio and combined 3 dB axial ratio and gain bandwidth compared to phase-rotation cells (PR), but at the cost of increased design complexity. Advanced antenna designs with optimized polarizer structures can mitigate this effect, but introduce additional complexity and cost.
reference_context: The reference context provides data on the performance of high-gain dual-band dual-CP antennas, including measurements of axial ratio, gain, and scanning loss for various frequencies and beam steering angles.
